summary_blocks.body: The 16 MBTI types are combinations of four preference pairs: Extraversion or Introversion (E/I), Sensing or Intuition (S/N), Thinking or Feeling (T/F), and Judging or Perceiving (J/P). If you already know your four letters, start from that type's profile. If you are deciding between two codes, compare the letters that actually differ. If your result carries an -A or -T, read the same-type comparison: those suffixes come from the NERIS Identity dimension used by 16Personalities, describe self-assessment and pressure response, and do not add types to the official MBTI framework.

sections.body_md:
### What Each of the Four Preference Pairs Describes

**E/I — Extraversion and Introversion:** where attention and energy more often turn — toward people and things outside, or toward ideas and reflection inside. When you genuinely have a choice, ask yourself: how do outside interaction and solitary reflection each change my attention and energy? Which activities leave me with something in reserve, and which ones need recovery time afterwards? Preferring solitude does not prove weak social skill, and speaking up readily does not rule out Introversion.

**S/N — Sensing and Intuition:** whether information gathering leans on concrete facts and experience, or on connections, patterns and possibilities. Ask: when I meet something new, do I look first at worked examples and steps, or first at how it connects to other things I know? Experience needs interpretation, and ideas need checking; neither letter ranks intelligence, creativity or depth of thought.

**T/F — Thinking and Feeling:** whether judgement starts from logical consistency and impersonal criteria, or from values and the effect on people. Ask: when I compare options, which criteria do I want stated, and whose needs do I want named? Both kinds of judgement can test evidence and weigh consequences; T does not mean uncaring, and F does not mean unanalytical.

**J/P — Judging and Perceiving:** whether outer life leans toward settled arrangements, or stays open to new information and options. Ask: what do I want decided in advance, and what do I want to keep learning about? Deadlines, tasks and roles make everyone plan and adjust; the letter does not measure conscientiousness, tidiness or planning skill.

### How to read a code and the directory groups

Each of the four positions takes one letter from one pair — INTP is I, N, T, P — and is not the sum of four ability scores. A profile explains how those descriptions read together, and also where they stop fitting.

The index groups the codes by NT, NF, SJ and SP. These labels combine two letters to make the 16 profiles easier to browse. Colours and nicknames such as "Logician" help you find a page; they are not a second measurement, and they guarantee nothing about occupation, intelligence, ethics or skill. Nicknames differ between sites, so compare by full code and by the framework in use.

### Name the question before you pick a route

| What you want to settle | Start here | What the page should give you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What the four letters mean, and how the whole description holds together | A base profile in the index below, such as [INTP](/en/personality/intp) | Letters, theoretical reading, work and relationship scenarios, practice and counterexamples, with no suffix required. |
| What the suffix in INTP-A or INTP-T is saying | [INTP-A](/en/personality/intp-a) or [INTP-T](/en/personality/intp-t) | The extended account of self-assessment, self-assurance and pressure response, including where it stops applying. |
| How A and T differ inside one type | [INTP-A vs INTP-T](/en/personality/intp-a-vs-intp-t) | Two readings of the same event, their costs and the questions worth asking next, without ranking ability. |
| Both base types sound like me — what should I compare | A cross-type comparison, such as [INTJ vs INTP](/en/personality/intj-vs-intp) or [ISFP vs INFP](/en/personality/isfp-vs-infp) | What J/P or S/N means in a real situation, without typing yourself by nickname, hobby or stress behaviour. |
| I want to answer a questionnaire and see a result | The [free MBTI test entry](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types) | The questionnaire and the explanation of results; the directory itself neither scores answers nor produces a result. |

### Browse by type: base profile, A/T guides and same-type comparison

The table covers the 16 four-letter types. Each type has a base profile, two suffix guides, and one comparison that sets the two ends against each other. Link text matches the page title, so you can confirm it in the site search box.

### Cross-type comparisons available here

A cross-type page does two things: it sets out the preferences the two codes share, then compares what each side tends to weigh in one shared situation. The list below covers the entries configured in this directory. For a pair that is not listed, read the two base profiles side by side and name the letter that really differs.

- [INTJ vs INTP](/en/personality/intj-vs-intp): both have I, N and T, so J/P and outer arrangement carry the comparison.
- [ENTJ vs INTJ](/en/personality/entj-vs-intj): both have N, T and J, so E/I attention and energy direction carry the comparison.
- [ESTJ vs ENTJ](/en/personality/estj-vs-entj): both have E, T and J, so S/N — fact and experience against pattern and possibility — carries the comparison.
- [ISTJ vs ISFJ](/en/personality/istj-vs-isfj): both have I, S and J, so the T/F basis for judgement carries the comparison.
- [ENFP vs ENTP](/en/personality/enfp-vs-entp): both have E, N and P, so T/F and the grounds for a decision carry the comparison.
- [INFJ vs INFP](/en/personality/infj-vs-infp): both have I, N and F, so J/P and the way an open question gets closed carry the comparison.
- [ISFP vs INFP](/en/personality/isfp-vs-infp): both have I, F and P, so the S/N preference for information carries the comparison.

### Keep the base code separate from A/T

A four-letter profile is readable on its own. A (Assertive) and T (Turbulent) belong to the Identity extension in the 16Personalities framework and describe self-assessment, self-assurance and response to pressure: A more often trusts its own judgement and is less unsettled by stress, while T more often doubts itself and reacts more strongly to pressure. That scale is not the official MBTI, and the final T is not the T (Thinking) inside the four-letter code.

The A/T pages here offer an educational reading and original scenarios. They cannot verify your own suffix result or predict mental health. Base profiles carry the full type description, suffix guides carry the extension, same-type comparisons carry A/T, and cross-type comparisons carry preferences that genuinely differ; the pages answer different questions, and nobody needs to read all of them in sequence. A code can lead you to the right explanation page, but recognising yourself in a description does not establish your type. Someone who reads INTP-T can start with the four preferences in the INTP profile and then read INTP-T; if the question is how A and T describe one event, go straight to the comparison instead of reading the base profile three times.

### When the type is unclear, keep the question and a counterexample

If several descriptions fit, write down the question you most want clarified, then read the matching base profile and any comparison that already exists. An original reading example: in one discussion you organise your points before speaking, in another you talk your way to clarity. What you compare is where attention and energy went, what the task required, and what you had already lived through — not a single behaviour taken as proof of I or E.

When a description feels familiar, also record a counterexample and ask separately:

- What actually happened?
- What did you notice or value?
- Which conditions shaped what you did?
- What would you be willing to try next time?

Different instruments, scoring methods and answering conditions change results; resonance or a change of label neither validates a test nor demonstrates lasting personality change. There is no need to retake a questionnaire until a label feels settled.

### Two types that differ by one letter: compare that letter

If you hesitate between ISTJ and ISFJ, read [ISTJ vs ISFJ](/en/personality/istj-vs-isfj) and compare the T/F basis behind a judgement. If you hesitate between ENFP and ENTP, read [ENFP vs ENTP](/en/personality/enfp-vs-entp), which also turns on T/F but uses a different situation. For ENTJ and INTJ, read [ENTJ vs INTJ](/en/personality/entj-vs-intj) and check E/I first rather than leadership. The INTJ–INTP and ISFP–INFP examples above compare J/P and S/N respectively. For ESTJ and ENTJ, read [ESTJ vs ENTJ](/en/personality/estj-vs-entj) and check how concrete information, experience and assumed patterns each get verified, rather than sorting the pair into doers and strategists. None of these entries turns a single answer into a typing rule.

Where no comparison exists, read the two base profiles as a pair and write down the letter that truly differs, plus the conditions you are still unsure about. There is no "best type" to hunt for on the strength of a nickname, and sharing letters is not the same as understanding another person completely.

### When you meet function shorthand, ask which explanation it belongs to

Terms such as Si, Ne, Ti or Fe on the base profiles come from type dynamics theory; "introverted" and "extraverted" in those abbreviations describe the attitude of a theoretical process, not whether someone was talking to people at that moment. Read the definition, the disagreement about the third process and the stated limits on the page first, then use the term to ask an observation question. A single function word cannot establish ability, a mechanism inside the brain, or the cause of a difficulty. A/T comes from a different framework and cannot be used to reorder cognitive functions either.

If the next step involves work or a relationship, keep going with the practical questions: actual tasks, skills, qualifications, workload, needs and boundaries. A personality page can help you organise that conversation; it cannot screen a job or a partner for you.

### A worked reading note: two results, one question to clarify

Suppose two instruments return ENTJ and INTJ, and what you actually want to know is when you turn outward more naturally and when you need to withdraw and sort things out. Record the instrument, its version and the situation you were answering from; leave what you cannot find as unknown rather than picking the nickname you prefer. Read the E/I parts of both profiles, then read [ENTJ vs INTJ](/en/personality/entj-vs-intj) with that question in hand, and keep the function shorthand at the theoretical level where it belongs.

Write down one occasion where you had room to choose: outlining alone made the problem easier to explain. Then write a counterexample: a question from someone else exposed a gap. If the work demanded an immediate reply, or if the material, staffing or your own fatigue were different that day, do not turn those conditions into a preference. You can agree with the people involved on sending material earlier next time and on a realistic response window, then check whether it helped; proposing an arrangement is not the same as having it accepted.

Reading can clarify a term, an unknown and one negotiable next step. It will not decide which instrument is accurate, demonstrate long-term personality change or grant competence for a role. If you only wanted the four letters, stop at the base profile; if the real question is the suffix, move to the matching A/T page. It is also fine to keep the question open instead of retaking a test for a fixed label.
sections.title: Choose the page that answers your question

items.answer:
Four preference pairs combine into 16 four-letter types. A count of 32 usually comes from counting the A and T ends separately under each code. A/T belongs to the NERIS Identity extension used by 16Personalities and is read separately from the four official preferences.

If you only want to understand one code, open its base profile in this directory. To compare suffixes, use the same-type A/T comparison; to separate two four-letter codes, start from the cross-type entries above. The number of links on this page says nothing about how many types the official framework contains.
items.question: Does MBTI Have 16 Types or 32?

items.answer:
Yes. The first column of the "Browse by type" table is the base profile, and it covers the four preferences, type theory, real situations and counterexamples. A/T is an optional extension from another framework, not a prerequisite for the four letters. Knowing your code also does not tell you your suffix.

If all you have is a four-letter result, read the base profile for that code first, then look at the related section at the end of the page, which points to the two suffix guides and the same-type comparison. Whether to continue depends on whether your question is about the four letters themselves or about how you react to feedback and pressure.
items.question: Can I read a page with only the four letters and no A/T?

items.answer:
The position changes the meaning. The third letter of INTP is T for Thinking, which belongs to the T/F judging preference; the -T after the hyphen is Turbulent, from the 16Personalities Identity extension. A person can read both descriptions, but they are not the same scale, and -T does not mean "more thinking".

When you check a report, look at the position: the third letter belongs to the four-letter code, and what follows the hyphen belongs to the suffix. If a report gives only four letters and no suffix field, it did not measure that dimension, so you cannot conclude whether you sit closer to A or T.
items.question: What Is the Difference Between the Two Ts in INTP-T?

items.answer:
No. Colours, groups and nicknames such as "Logician" or "Commander" help you navigate; they do not measure ability or occupational qualification. Nicknames differ between sites, so search by full code and framework. Analysis, leadership, care and creative work depend on training, experience, task conditions and actual performance.

There is also a sourcing difference: many English nicknames come from 16Personalities, and the same code may carry a different name elsewhere. They work as memory hooks, not as hiring criteria.
items.question: Do nicknames and colours prove career ability?

items.answer:
First check whether the same instrument, the same version and the same scoring interpretation were used, then look at the answering conditions and the uncertainty in each result. With too little information you cannot decide which one is more accurate. Sharing letters across sites does not make two scales equivalent, and preferring a result or feeling that a description fits does not make it the correct answer. Keep both readings and their counterexamples instead of retesting for a fixed label.

If two results differ by one letter, work through the comparison page for that letter and use one shared situation to see which basis each side weighs. If they differ by two letters or more, it is usually more useful to check the language of the items, the circumstances you answered from and recent pressure than to pick the label that feels more like you.
items.question: My results from different tests disagree — which should I believe?

items.answer:
It cannot give a match score or a competence verdict. A comparison page turns preferences that genuinely differ into questions about information, judgement, arrangement or feedback. In a relationship you still need to learn needs, consent, boundaries and actual behaviour; at work you still have to check tasks, skills, qualifications, opportunities and constraints. Choosing one concrete next step and watching what happens is more useful than deciding about people by type.

The value of a comparison is a shared vocabulary: when two people handle the same thing differently, the dimensions on the page let each say which basis matters to them, instead of using a type to define the other person.
items.question: Can a personality comparison tell me about compatibility or career choice?

items.answer:
The pages give the official framework description, theoretical explanation, original studies or research reviews, and state what each can support; work, relationship and practice scenarios are marked as original educational examples. Studies have to be read with their instrument, sample and year in view, and evidence supporting one version of the MBTI does not automatically validate the FermatMind assessment or A/T. Read the sources and method boundaries with the unproven parts in mind as well.

Each page ends with a sources section naming the studies it cites and the scope they cover. Where a claim rests on framework description without a matching study, the page says it is theoretical. When you meet a percentage, prediction or match score with no source, treat it as unverified.
items.question: Do these pages have scientific backing and original sources?

sections.body_md:
The official MBTI describes four preference pairs. A/T belongs to a separate extension; sharing letters does not make different instruments equivalent. Type descriptions and cognitive functions are theoretical readings, not established psychological mechanisms.

McCrae and Costa (1989) compared the 1985 MBTI with NEO-PI self-reports and peer ratings in 267 men and 201 women aged 19–93; the abstract does not describe a nationally representative sample. Their analysis did not support true dichotomies or qualitatively distinct types, and found overlap with several dimensions of the five-factor model. Instrument versions and samples cannot be mixed: the publisher describes later revisions, and this page does not establish the reliability or validity of FermatMind scores. That specific study cannot validate the scenarios here, determine an individual's type, or settle every question raised by later instruments.

Erford et al. (2025) separately reviewed 193 studies published between 1999 and 2024 that used the English MBTI Form M, reporting good internal consistency (0.845–0.921) and convergent evidence with similar constructs; among the included literature there was no independent structural validity or test–retest study beyond the manual. Consistency of scores does not confirm natural types, and it does not validate A/T or transfer to the FermatMind assessment. Supporting evidence and research gaps both have to be read against a specific instrument and sample.

The scenarios and exercises on this page are original educational examples, not clinical guidance or population findings. Use them against your own experience and counterexamples; a type alone cannot diagnose, hire, select a career or screen a partner.

English text revised 20 November 2026. This page is an educational synthesis based on the sources listed and does not claim independent clinical review.

- [The Myers-Briggs Company: MBTI facts and scope](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts)
- [16Personalities: the NERIS framework and A/T](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory)
- [McCrae and Costa (1989): MBTI and the five-factor model](https://scholars.duke.edu/publication/1458465)
- [Erford et al. (2025): MBTI Form M psychometric review](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcad.70006)
- [The Myers & Briggs Foundation: MBTI Code of Ethics](https://www.myersbriggs.org/using-type-as-a-professional/mbti-code-of-ethics/home.htm)
- [The Myers & Briggs Foundation: the four preference pairs](https://www.myersbriggs.org/my-mbti-personality-type/the-mbti-preferences/)

The FermatMind assessment uses its own item bank and scoring; the scope is set out in the [scoring and evidence note](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).
